metadata.title: Building 2D Particle Effects in Godot
metadata.series_title: Particle Systems and VFX in Godot
metadata.lecture_opening_description: Build a burst and a trail you can reuse

beats.narration_text: Particle Systems and VFX in Godot. Building 2D Particle Effects in Godot. Build, trigger, and test a burst and a continuous effect.

shot.motion: hold

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. How do we make particles behave on purpose? We will connect emission, motion, and drawing, then test the effect through the input that uses it.

shot.motion: component animation

qc.sparse_reason: The required hesitant writer corrects one misconception; deliberate sparse bookend.

beats.narration_text: Emitter. The source of new particles. Material. A resource that controls behavior or drawing. Signal. A notification that something happened. Lifetime. How long one particle remains alive.

shot.motion: component animation

terms.meaning: A resource that controls behavior or drawing
How long one particle remains alive

beats.narration_text: This is our test arena: one marker, a dark half, and a light half. Keep those references steady. A useful particle effect has to read at the size and contrast where the game will use it.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Add G P U Particles Two D to the arena. The node controls how many particles exist and when they are born. Its empty process slot is the next part of the construction, not evidence that the effect is finished.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Create a Particle Process Material in that slot. This resource owns motion and variation. Turn Disable Z on, so this two-dimensional effect stays in its plane. The node and its resource answer different questions.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: The first particles are tiny. Assign our procedural soft-dot texture and they become legible. This is the draw part of the effect. A running simulation can be difficult to see when its visible mark is missing.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Set the launch direction upward, with negative Y. Give it a speed range from one hundred to two hundred twenty. New particles rise away from the marker. Speed changes travel; it does not change how many are born.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Gravity is positive one hundred forty on Y. The launch begins upward, then bends down. Set gravity to zero for a straight comparison. Restore it before changing the burst schedule, so we can still explain the difference.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Now inspect the resource and the node separately. Direction, gravity, and speed live in the process material. Amount, lifetime, and one shot live on the particle node. Looking in the right place makes tuning much less mysterious.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Keep the texture fixed and move the same effect across both backgrounds. Its pale center reads differently against the light area. We are checking visibility, not changing the physics to compensate for a drawing problem.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Turn One Shot on. Restart the emitter and watch one complete emission cycle. It stops making new particles, while the existing particles finish their lives. One shot alone does not make every particle appear at the same instant.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Set Explosiveness to one and restart. The particles now arrive together, giving the event a crisp onset. Compare it with zero, where births are distributed through the cycle. This control changes timing, not the texture.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Open spread to one hundred eighty degrees. The burst expands around its origin. Narrow it to twenty-five and it points like a small spray. Pick the silhouette that communicates the event, then keep that choice consistent.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Forty-eight particles make this burst. Double the amount and replay it, then return to forty-eight. The denser result is not automatically clearer. Count is a design control, and it is only one part of rendering cost.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Attach the size curve. Each particle starts small, grows quickly, and shrinks toward its exit. The curve follows normalized lifetime, so the same shape applies to every particle even when the overall lifetime changes.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Attach the color ramp. A pale hot center gives way to orange and then zero alpha. The gradual fade belongs to the drawing, while lifetime still controls when the particle dies. Those two endings should agree.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Lengthen lifetime from eight tenths to one point four seconds and replay. The particles have more time to travel. Restore eight tenths for this pickup: a short event needs a short, readable acknowledgement, rather than a lingering cloud.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Save the burst as its own scene, initially inactive. Give its visibility rectangle room for the full path. The saved resource now carries the emission, motion, and drawing choices together, ready for a trigger to instantiate it.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: This is the trigger code. Space instantiates the saved scene at the marker’s position. The finished signal removes that temporary instance. We keep a count because a good-looking burst can still leave an invisible owner behind.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Run the arena and press Space through its ordinary input path. These inputs are scripted for the recording. Watch the burst complete, then the instance counter return to zero. The result comes from the same scene we just saved.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Move the marker left and trigger again. Then move right and repeat. Each instance gets the event’s current position. The scene is reusable because it contains the effect, while the caller supplies where and when it belongs.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Here is a staged ownership fault. Put the burst beneath the marker, then hide the marker on activation. The event still creates an instance, but its parent hides the picture. Emission does not guarantee visibility.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Repair the owner: place the effect under the visible arena. Leave the marker hidden and trigger again. The burst now survives the marker’s visibility change. Choose an owner whose lifetime matches the visual job, rather than the object that happened to trigger it.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.narration_text: Reset, then trigger repeatedly. Each finished instance cleans itself up, so the counter comes back to zero. This checks ownership and cleanup. It does not prove that every future game event will call the effect at the right moment.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.act: Turn A Burst Into A Stream
beats.narration_text: Stop play and duplicate the particle node as Trail. Make its process material unique before editing. The texture can remain shared. Sharing an image is useful; accidentally sharing the motion settings would retune the pickup as well.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed

beats.act: Turn A Burst Into A Stream
beats.narration_text: Turn One Shot off and Explosiveness down to zero. The trail now produces a steady stream. Give it a two-second lifetime and forty-eight particles. At steady state, amount divided by lifetime describes its nominal birth rate.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed
shot.visual_intent: Turn A Burst Into A Stream

beats.act: Turn A Burst Into A Stream
beats.narration_text: Aim the trail upward, narrow the spread, and remove gravity. A slow speed range makes rising embers. We have changed the visual job from a momentary acknowledgement to an ongoing condition, using the same basic particle machinery.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed
shot.visual_intent: Turn A Burst Into A Stream

beats.act: Turn A Burst Into A Stream
beats.narration_text: Move the source with local coordinates off. Newly born particles follow the marker, while older ones remain in world space. Turn local coordinates on and the existing cloud moves with its source. That difference decides whether you get a trail or an attached aura.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed
shot.visual_intent: Turn A Burst Into A Stream

beats.act: Turn A Burst Into A Stream
beats.narration_text: Turn the stream condition off. New births stop, and the existing embers finish. Turn it on to resume. A continuous effect needs a condition that can become false; restarting it every frame is not a substitute for that condition.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed
shot.visual_intent: Turn A Burst Into A Stream

beats.act: Turn A Burst Into A Stream
beats.narration_text: Inspect the visibility rectangle around the moving trail. A tiny bound may cull a still-visible effect when its emitter leaves the view. Keep a conservative box for the measured motion, and test it with the actual camera rather than guessing from the origin.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed
shot.visual_intent: Turn A Burst Into A Stream

beats.act: Turn A Burst Into A Stream
beats.narration_text: Convert a duplicate to C P U Particles Two D. The settings now live directly on the node. Compare the visible result, then choose for your target and required features. Conversion is a starting point; GPU-specific features still need an explicit check.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed
shot.visual_intent: Turn A Burst Into A Stream

beats.act: Turn A Burst Into A Stream
beats.narration_text: Save the continuous scene and the test arena. The pickup has a real input trigger and finished cleanup; the trail has a condition and a deliberate coordinate space. Those contracts make the effects useful outside this demonstration.

shot.motion: Genuine native editor actions and particles at original speed
shot.visual_intent: Turn A Burst Into A Stream

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A visible effect needs emission, motion, and drawing. Burst timing and lifetime have different jobs. Curves shape appearance over each particle’s age. A visible owner and finished cleanup make triggers reliable. A stream follows a condition and a coordinate space. Reusable scenes still need tests on their target.
